title: US Agencies Urge Organizations to Harden Refrigeration Controllers
content_md: The US government is urging healthcare, chemical, food, and transportation organizations to harden their industrial refrigeration and cold chain monitoring systems. Over the past weeks, threat actors have been hacking monitoring systems to tamper with fridges and freezers in supermarkets and blood banks across Europe, causing millions in losses. Hundreds of supermarkets were hit on October 11, when the attackers turned the temperatures in fridges to 50 degrees Celsius (122 degrees Fahrenheit) and set freezers to defrost, spoiling food and, in some cases, causing fires. A second wave of attacks hit more than 100 supermarkets and a blood bank this week, but only supermarkets suffered losses. Quick action from staff prevented the compromise of blood products and samples, the French Blood Establishment (EFS) said. Russian hacktivist groups such as Noname057(16) and Z-Pentest Alliance reportedly claimed hacking Danfoss, leading to speculation that they mounted the supermarket attacks. However, nothing has been confirmed, and Iranian hacktivists or state-sponsored hackers may also be responsible, BBC notes .
